newsitem.title: USA: Tosco sees early summer Trainer restart.
newsitem.headline: Tosco sees early summer Trainer restart.

text.p: Tosco Corp said Tuesday it expects to restart its second Philadelphia area refinery early this summer when it sees an improving products market.
"At present, margins are weak all across the U.S., but overall industry prospects appear more positive than they have for some time," Tosco said.

"Tosco's $100 million refurbishment and modernization program at its Trainer Refinery in Pennsylvania is on schedule and on budget," the company said. "We expect Trainer to restart early this summer and be extremely competitive in its marketplace, with cash operating costs below $2.00 per barrel."
Last year, Tosco reached an agreement with organized labor at the refinery -- formerly known as British Petroleum Co Plc's Marcus Hook refinery.
Toscao acquired the 150,000 barrel per day plant in February when it purchased BP's U.S. Northeast marketing and refining assets for $59 million.
